verdicts.why: Excessive pride read as soft, faintly ridiculous self-admiration matches the gloss, the conceit contrast stays inside the word, and both examples are this sense.
Rescue from harm or danger is exactly the gloss, and the grandeur/urgency claim plus the uncle-as-encourager contrast describe the word's force rather than its users or origin.
Backing or speaking up for something is the gloss's supports-or-champions sense, and the approving charge fits it.
Defining her by her tie to one man tracks the gloss's parenthetical, the possessive edge is plausibly negative, and the his-woman examples fit this sense.
Reading the superlative as setting the beloved above all others is a description of the word's force for this endearment sense, not an origin story.
The note reproduces the gloss's two-way relation (loves or is loved) and the neutral charge and examples fit.
Founder-as-parent of the institution is this gloss's sense, the respectful positive charge fits, and all three examples are founders.
Closeness defined by confided private matters is precisely the gloss, and the companion contrast stays inside the word.
Fellow membership of a union or sorority turned into a family tie between women is the gloss, and the union-sisters example fits.
Position defined by cohabitation and the man's standing matches the gloss, and a negative charge is plausible for a woman kept in that subordinate place.
Ongoing affair outside marriage with blame built in is the adulterous-woman gloss, the concubine contrast is within the word, and the example fits.
Pet name for any old woman, grandmother or not, is the gloss; familiar-versus-respectful is a register contrast and shrinking her to her age supports the negative charge.
Ugly, evil-looking old woman met with disgust and mockery is the gloss, and the witch contrast (fear versus contempt) stays inside the word.
Said to an elderly woman as address and lending her family standing is this gloss, and the example is a direct address.
Person made and aimed by another at unpleasant or dishonest jobs is the gloss, the tool contrast is within the word, and the creature-of-the-duke example fits.
Controlled person whose dishonest acts belong to whoever pulls the strings is the gloss, with scorn and mockery matching the negative charge.
A thing picked up for dirty or unpleasant jobs and valued only for use is the gloss's controlled-person sense, and coldness is a force claim not a distribution claim.
Not belonging in this environment while possibly belonging elsewhere is the gloss, the neutral charge fits, and the village example is this sense.
Reputation as a plain container that takes whatever gets attached is the gloss, neutral fits, and the good-name examples are this sense.
High esteem and honor with a formal register label matches the gloss and the positive charge.
Disgrace or shame with blame heard in it is the gloss, the shame contrast stays inside the word, and the examples (brought reproach, without reproach) fit this sense.
